problem: Existing VLN-CE agents do not explicitly exploit the landmarks and their temporal/spatial order in instructions, and their visual perception is weakly tied to the instruction, which leads to inaccurate and long trajectories.
motivation: Humans navigate by recognizing landmarks and their spatial relationships. Making these landmarks explicit in both reasoning and perception should give better grounding and more efficient navigation in continuous environments.
key_idea: Use a language model to extract landmarks and their temporal order from the instruction into a directed graph, then use it to guide landmark-aware multimodal perception (semantic-depth fusion, distance-based masking, cross-attention with RGB) feeding the policy.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract suggests that structured landmark reasoning combined with semantic and depth cues improves both success and path efficiency (shorter trajectory length).
method: Landmark graph extraction: a language model extracts semantic landmarks and their temporal order from the instruction and builds a structured directed graph guiding reasoning and perception.
View expansion: expands the visual observations to improve visual understanding.
Semantic-depth fusion: fuses semantic segmentation and depth cues with an SE (squeeze-and-excitation) attention mechanism.
Dynamic distance-based masking: modulates landmark features by distance with a dynamic mask.
Cross-attention fusion: fuses landmark features with RGB embeddings via cross-attention.
Policy network: takes the fused multimodal representation for decision-making.
